source.title: Mission 15 — Consumer Automation — Season II

labels.name: source:h2
labels.description: Demand exposed by Telegraph Hackathon Season II

source.body:
**Start with the customer and work backwards.** This mission is about delivering something useful, not accumulating disconnected Intents or registrations. A contributor can build the whole solution—application, intelligence Provider and relevant evaluation work—or concentrate on one part and work with others. All three hackathon tracks are open, with separate qualifying entries under the [official rules](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/rules).

## The opportunity

**Who it serves:** Consumers, travelers and online shoppers with permissioned digital agents.

**Problem:** Refund requests are tedious to evidence and checkout bots act on stale stock or price data.

**A useful result:** A permissioned refund/claim workflow with proof or a purchase agent that acts only on verified stock/price and a user-defined budget.

Pick a specific customer and workflow. Establish the alternative they use today, a realistic willingness-to-pay or budget constraint, a measurable result, acceptable error and response time. These are example opportunities, not exclusive products or confirmed customers. See [Consumer Automation](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/missions/consumer-automation) and the [full mission catalogue](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/missions).

| Route | Actual outcome to build | Shared capability families to investigate and use |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Automated refund or SLA claim** | Read a passenger-authorized itinerary or uptime contract, buy disruption/SLA evidence and draft or send a claim only with explicit permission. | `TRAVEL_DISRUPTION`, `SERVER_UPTIME_MONITOR`, `SLA_COMPLIANCE`, `CONTRACT_OBLIGATION_AUDIT` |
| **2. Verified price-and-stock purchase** | Use live SKU/price intelligence to decide whether a budgeted checkout condition is met; request explicit approval before a real purchase. | `LIVE_SHELF_PRICE`, `SKU_IN_STOCK`, `COMMERCE_PURCHASE_VERIFY` |
| **3. Two-agent authenticity check** | Two controlled agents buy URL safety/product-authenticity intelligence and make a simulated payment or authorized testnet transaction. | `URL_SAFE`, `PRODUCT_AUTHENTICITY`, `CRYPTO_TRANSFER_VERIFY` |

**First milestone:** one realistic input → a paid Telegraph intelligence request → a checked result with its source/uncertainty → a useful action or answer → receipt and total cost. Include one failure case before expanding the workflow. You do **not** need to implement all three example products.

**Tests worth demonstrating:** Test stale stock, wrong price, cancelled flight with missing evidence and rejected user authorization; never complete irreversible checkout without consent.

**Measures that matter:** Cost per completed claim or validated checkout, false stock signal rate, user effort saved and avoidable purchases prevented.

## Intelligence needed

**Published starting families:** `TRAVEL_DISRUPTION`, `SLA_COMPLIANCE`, `SERVER_UPTIME_MONITOR`, `LIVE_SHELF_PRICE`, `SKU_IN_STOCK`, `URL_SAFE`, `PRODUCT_AUTHENTICITY`, `COMMERCE_PURCHASE_VERIFY`, `DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY`.

These are shared network capabilities, **not separate bounties** created for this mission. The same capability may support several missions, with one canonical Intent, one Provider market and one evaluation pool. The list is a starting map, not a mandatory bill of materials or proof of live coverage.

Before implementing anything, inspect the [live canonical Intent list](https://devnode.telegraphprotocol.com/engine/v1/intents), [request and response schemas](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/intent-schema), [ranked Providers](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/explore) and [published Intent catalogue](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/blob/main/docs/INTENTS.md). Use the **exact** live `intent_name` and `request.params`; family names and guessed `_GENERAL` suffixes are not reliable request identifiers. Some unknown names return HTTP 200 with a null schema, which is not a working Intent. The [mission mapping](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/blob/main/docs/MISSIONS.md) is helpful for discovery, but the node determines which capabilities are callable and what evaluation path applies.

A finished report, dashboard, refund, memo or decision is usually **application composition**, not a new protocol Intent. Use existing reusable capabilities first. Only propose a new Intent for genuinely reusable intelligence missing from the catalogue.

## Ways to contribute

### Apps & Agents — deliver the product

Build a runnable application that **autonomously purchases or sells intelligence through Telegraph** and uses the response to complete a meaningful task. Start with the smallest useful customer workflow; confirm the supporting Intents and live Provider quality before committing to an architecture.

Choose the right [delivery path](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/inference-paths): [Engine Ask](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/engine-ask) for fresh on-demand work; [x402](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/x402-inference) or [escrow](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/escrow-inference) for supported settlement; [WebSocket Signals](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/websocket-signals) when reusable streamed intelligence is appropriate; [MCP](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/mcp-server) for integrations. A Signal subscription is not a substitute for a fresh, user-specific check. A 402 payment challenge is not evidence of a completed purchase.

Make uncertainty visible. Handle partial or conflicting answers, stale data, missing Providers, spending limits and failures. Prove the total **cost per useful completed outcome** rather than multiplying paid requests unnecessarily. Reuse valid fresh intelligence when permitted; avoid paying repeatedly for the same shared fact. Irreversible transactions and sensitive actions require the user's authorization. Simulated or testnet behavior must be labelled as such.

**Completion evidence:** runnable app and instructions, a new realistic input producing a useful result, authentic Telegraph request/payment evidence, costs and latency, and a reproducible failure case. A static interface or a Miner registration alone does not qualify as the app.

### Miners / Providers — supply the intelligence

Identify a missing or weak capability for this customer workflow. Test existing Providers to understand the quality bar. Independent competing implementations for the same canonical Intent are welcome; show how yours performs in accuracy, coverage, freshness, price, reliability or latency. Implement a callable service for a supported canonical Intent, following its actual request/response schema and [Miner YAML guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/yaml-config).

Check the [validation guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/validation-api) and current [registration steps](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/miner-registration). **Known documentation limitation (Nov 15):** the guide says its `POST /dashboard/validate` endpoint currently returns 404; use the available web checks, documented local checks and supported registration dry-run instead of treating that POST as working. Use the [faucet](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/faucet) for eligible testnet needs. Confirm the registration is active and the service answers the actual Intent; capture its registration ID, test cases, measured results and paid request evidence. Distinguish direct diagnostic requests from selection by ranked routing.

Share working endpoints and registration IDs here so other applications and missions can reuse the Provider.

### Evaluators — measure whether the intelligence is good

Use the selected Intent's **actual node class, family and scoring path**, not the name or an old bounty description, to determine what's needed:

- **Deterministic:** reliable public truth-source material and the supported comparator path. A new judgment adapter is not inherently required.
- **Hybrid:** the checkable truth source/comparator and judgment contribution that the live scoring path actually uses.
- **Judgment:** sourced, balanced better/worse examples and a compatible evaluation adapter **where needed**. Do not assume every Intent needs a new adapter plus material.

Contribute through [Anjoman Evaluate](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/eval), following [material formats and provenance](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/contribute-evaluation-data) and the [scoring-module guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/build-a-scoring-module) when applicable. Use primary evidence, timestamps, block/chain or jurisdiction identifiers, correct units and tolerances. Include correct, incorrect, incomplete and ambiguous cases; avoid datasets solvable merely by answer length, keywords or copied prompt wording. Test on unseen sources and failure types. Confirm **eligible / rejected** material state and actual module status separately; passing a local test or uploading rows does not imply canonical promotion.

A single project may contribute a working app, a Provider and genuinely useful evaluation work. Each track still requires its own qualifying evidence. No extra or duplicative component is needed simply to claim participation across all three.

## Share work here as it happens

**Read the latest comments and existing [Bounties Issues](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/issues) to understand current activity, available capabilities and opportunities to collaborate.** Multiple contributors are welcome to independently build applications, Providers and Evaluators for the same mission or Intent, including competing implementations. Existing work does not reserve a mission, product or Intent. Share progress and findings so others can collaborate, reuse useful contributions or compete independently.

If using the existing Bounties workflow, post `/claim` and then a short comment identifying your scope. Claims are **non-exclusive**. Keep the thread current with `/progress <update>` at least every **72 hours** while claimed, and link relevant work from other mission threads. Useful updates include:

```text
Scope: [product or capability + customer problem]
Track(s): [Apps & Agents / Miners / Providers / Evaluators]
Working on: [concrete deliverable, canonical Intents if known]
Reusing (optional): [existing work, Providers, evaluations + links]
Approach: [what you are building and how you plan to deliver it]
Current state: [building / tested / blocked / submitted]
Proof or next milestone: [repo/demo/endpoint, reproducible result]
```

When ready, post `/submit <links and evidence>` for your individual contribution, **and** use the official Anjoman submission path. GitHub comments coordinate work; they are not the final hackathon entry or evaluation upload. One team's submission does not close the mission to other participants. Existing accepted contributions and claims remain valid; reviewers assess individual entries separately. Don't post credentials, private customer data, protected evaluation samples or sensitive exploit details.

## Prove it, share it, submit it

A strong entry can be tested by someone outside the team: provide a live demo or callable endpoint, public-safe repository, run instructions, real request IDs/receipts, one failure test, honest cost figures and limitations. For apps, explain what was purchased and **what useful action happened afterward**. Consider listing working apps in [Anjoman Apps](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/apps) for others to discover.

The [Season II judging rules](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/rules) apply across all three tracks (100 points each; **70/100** overall and each track's stated technical minimum). Apps are scored on technical quality/mainnet readiness (35 points, minimum 24), commercial viability (25), independent adoption (10), integration and usage (5), reproducibility (5), and organic growth/developer activation (20). Providers and Evaluators have their **own** track rubrics on the same rules page.

The 20 growth points cover **useful education (5), ease of adoption (5), organic distribution (5), and independent community activation (5)**. Share a working explanation or video, a genuinely useful walkthrough, and **at least three meaningful original progress updates on separate dates**. Invite independent developers to try, reproduce or integrate your work; show their real feedback and results. Publish where relevant (GitHub, Discord, X, technical communities) and follow the published tagging/link guidance. Bought engagement, fake traffic, manipulated stars, self-dealing and fabricated demand do not count. **Star the [Bounties repository](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties)** as required in Section 5; this is an entry requirement, not proof of growth.

**Prizes and possible earnings:** $7,000 for the Season II main competition ($3,000 Apps, $2,000 Providers, $2,000 Evaluators), plus $3,000 reserved for separate December challenges—not an extra automatic Season II pool. Awards depend on eligibility and verification. Beyond prizes, eligible Providers may earn from paid usage, Evaluator contributions may earn applicable protocol rewards, and products may generate revenue if customers adopt them. **Nothing is guaranteed** by a claim, registration or testnet call. This is a coordination Issue, not a separately funded GitHub bounty.

**Deadline:** **December 1, 2026, 23:59 UTC** for the main competition; **November 20** is the progress showcase. Finish the [official H2 submission](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon) using its live form when available, selecting the tracks and attaching distinct evidence for each. As of November 15, the site says the final form opens later; don't mistake a GitHub `/submit` comment for the final submission. The official rules control eligibility, awards, dates and any subsequent announcements.

## Before reporting a blocker

| Problem | Check first |
|---|---|
| Intent request fails or returns an empty schema | Select an exact live canonical Intent; inspect `request.params`, response fields and active Provider coverage in the [schema guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/intent-schema). A 200 response with `request: null` is not a valid Intent. |
| No result after x402 or escrow | Follow the documented full payment flow; a 402 offer alone is not a settled purchase. Check available receipt and account evidence. |
| A Miner looks highly ranked but answers the wrong question | Reproduce the input, preserve the raw/shaped result and actual receipt, compare with a direct diagnostic call, and report the specific ranking gap. |
| Registration, validation or bond trouble | Check the registration and validation docs, live node state, chain configuration and [faucet](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/faucet); the documented `POST /dashboard/validate` route is currently flagged as broken. |
| Evaluation material or module rejected | Check eligible/rejected reasons, provenance, required shape, supported family kind and public scoring requirements; don't infer adapter requirements from an Intent's label. |
| A similar app or capability already exists | Independent competing implementations are welcome. Review existing work for useful references, reuse or collaborate where appropriate, or proceed independently. No exclusive claims. |

For a genuine unresolved protocol defect, post a concise reproducible report here (exact Intent, public request, expected/actual behavior and safe evidence), then use [Discord](https://discord.gg/telegraphprotocol) for escalation if necessary.

## Done when

- [ ] A real customer need and runnable app/agent that solves it are demonstrated.
- [ ] A supported paid Telegraph request/sale leads to a useful action, with authentic receipt/accounting evidence.
- [ ] Relevant shared Intents have usable Provider supply and evaluation coverage, or precisely documented remaining gaps.
- [ ] A reviewer can reproduce a realistic success and failure case, including total cost and latency.
- [ ] Contributors' progress and relevant final entries are linked in comments; evidence distinguishes testnet, production and genuine external adoption.

This checklist measures **mission coverage**, not one person's prize eligibility. A successful app does not imply every possible workflow or every mapped Intent is complete. Keep this Issue available for distinct contributors; do not close it merely because one scope finished.

## Reward

**No standalone GitHub payout.** Season II prizes and ongoing protocol earnings are separate and governed by their published eligibility and payment terms.
